entities.summary:
The Vanuatu Football Federation (VFF), established in 1934, serves as the governing body for football in Vanuatu, an island nation in the South Pacific Ocean. Headquartered in Port Vila, the VFF is a member of both the Oceania Football Confederation (OFC) and FIFA, the global governing body of football. This institution plays a crucial role in promoting the sport within Vanuatu and providing a platform for local talent to compete internationally. The federation's establishment marked a significant moment in the country's sporting history, as it laid the foundation for organized football, fostering national identity and pride among Vanuatu's diverse communities.

Since its inception, the VFF has overseen the development of football throughout the islands, organizing local leagues and national teams that have participated in regional competitions. The VFF was instrumental in Vanuatu's participation in the OFC Nations Cup, where the national team first competed in 1973. Over the decades, the federation has worked to enhance the standards of coaching, player development, and facilities, contributing to a gradual improvement in the quality of football in the region. Notable achievements include Vanuatu's surprising run to the semifinals of the 2016 OFC Nations Cup, showcasing the growing competitiveness of its national team on the international stage.
